author: Eric Hess
releaseNotes: Faster frame handling (fewer database writes and cross-device calls), and saving the app no longer reconnects unless a connection setting changed. New: open and bypassed zone lists (per partition when you assign zones to partitions), a trouble summary and an optional UNO Status device; last alarm type and zone; arm with bypass; zone low-battery and lost-supervision attributes; stale sensor report; zone timer dump; keypad sounds (with diagnostic events); notification quiet hours, partition filter, repeat suppression and a connection-lost alert; a 30 second keepalive option (the heartbeat setting is now Keepalive) and a configurable command timeout. The event history is kept in memory and rebuilt from its attribute after a restart, and lastSystemMessage is removed (frame 09 is a keypad sound). A number too long to be valid in a zone, partition or PGM setting no longer breaks setup. Each part of a Contact ID event (raw string, code, qualifier, partition, zone, user) is now its own attribute for rules, and replayed (qualifier 6) events are shown as reports. A truncated frame no longer costs the frame after it, and the receive buffer is capped. A failed send now reconnects instead of leaving a command stuck, and a damaged Contact ID event or acknowledgement is dropped instead of being read as a different one. Open zones now come with a count and the time each opened (`openZonesTimed`, `openZonesDetail`), and an option keeps a zone that was open when bypassed in the list. The partition device has a new armingMode attribute: the UNO's exit-delay state doesn't say stay or away, so it reports what was requested instead of the previous arm's mode. A wider range of socket failure messages is now recognised, host information is requested at login, the password and master code inputs are masked, and the UNO's firmware is checked against the minimum the TPI document lists (firmwareWarning, also shown in the app's Status section). 1.3.1: a reply that reached the hub before the command was saved as sent no longer causes a needless retry (or, for commands that are not retried, a reconnect), the connection driver no longer tries to connect before it has an address, and a new Device name prefix setting puts a prefix in front of every partition and zone label. Zones can now be named and typed one by one in the app, with the UNO's own name shown for each and a button to load those names before setup is finished, and a zone renamed on the Devices page keeps its name when the app is saved. 1.4.0: the partition and zone devices are now children of the UNO Connection device, so the Devices page lists them indented under it (Hubitat only nests a device under another device, and an app's children are listed separately). The connection device now creates, names and updates them, the app tells it what they should be, and a new Sync devices command on it does the same on demand. The first Done after upgrading removes the old zone and partition devices and makes new ones with the same ids, and a zone keeps its old name, so a rule, tile or Maker API entry that used one must be pointed at the new device. Update all drivers and the app together.
